### **Research questions**

Linear regression: Can we predict how much someone trusts politicians based on their education, age, political interest and income?

Logistic regression: Can we predict if someone voted based on their education, age, political interest and income?

### **Data pre-processing**

```{r}
#| output: false

# setup R library's and working directories
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)

# Define variables pointing to the relevant directories
dataDir <- "data"
outDir <- "output"
figDir <- "figures"
```

#### **Changing names**

```{r}
# Read csv and store it in the data variable. 
full_data <- read.csv(here::here(dataDir, "ESS11e04_2.csv"))

```

Current size of the data-set: `{r} nrow(full_data)` rows and `{r} ncol(full_data)` columns.

```{r}
# Select the columns we will need and store it in a new table based on the codebook.
relevant_data <- select(full_data, trstplt, agea, eisced, hinctnta, polintr, vote)

# Rename columns so the names are more readable based on the codebook
relevant_data <- rename(relevant_data, 
			 age = agea,
		   trust.in.politicians = trstplt,
			 education = eisced, 
			 household.income = hinctnta, 
			 political.interest = polintr,
			 vote = vote
			 )
```

#### **NA - encoding**

| Missing Value Encoding | Meaning of Encoding       |
|------------------------|---------------------------|
| 55                     | Other                     |
| 66                     | Not applicable            |
| 7, 77                  | Refusal of Anwser         |
| 8, 88                  | Don't know                |
| 9, 99, 999             | Missing Value             |
| 3                      | Not eligible (only vote)  |

The data set contains several codes that represent responses that do not represent meaningful values for our analysis. We will re-code them as missing values

For trust.in.politicians, household.income and education the values we filter by are: 55, 66, 77, 88 and 99.

```{r}
filter_values <- c(55, 66, 77, 88, 99) 

relevant_data <- 
	relevant_data |>
	mutate(trust.in.politicians = replace(trust.in.politicians, trust.in.politicians %in% filter_values, NA)) |>
	mutate(household.income = replace(household.income, household.income %in% filter_values, NA)) |>
	mutate(education = replace(education, education %in% filter_values, NA))

```

For vote and political.interest the values we mutate are: 7,8 and 9.

```{r}
filter_values = c(7,8,9)

relevant_data <- 
	relevant_data|> 
	mutate(vote = replace(vote, vote %in% filter_values, NA)) |>
	mutate(political.interest = replace(political.interest, political.interest %in% filter_values, NA))

```

For age the value we mutate is: 999, vote the value 3

```{r}
relevant_data <- mutate(relevant_data, age = replace(age, age == 999, NA))
relevant_data <- mutate(relevant_data, vote = replace(vote, vote == 3, NA))
```

Current size of the data-set after selection and filtering: `{r} nrow(relevant_data)` rows and `{r} ncol(relevant_data)` columns.
